headline: 30 Bangladeshis return home from Cambodian detention centre
summary: The workers had been trapped in scam centres before being detained by immigration police in Phnom Penh.
details: Thirty Bangladeshi workers have returned to Dhaka after being released from the Immigration Detention Centre in Phnom Penh, Cambodia.
The workers arrived at Shahjalal International Airport on Tuesday afternoon via a Thai Airways flight.
They had originally traveled to Cambodia in search of employment but became trapped in scam centres within the country.
While the Cambodian government offered repatriation without fines, immigration police detained 32 people during checks on September 3.
Two individuals were released, while the remaining 30 were held in the detention centre due to irregular status and other complications.

Following diplomatic efforts and the completion of required procedures, the 30 workers were finally secured and repatriated.
caption:
Trapped in scam centres and then detained by police, 30 Bangladeshis have finally returned home from Cambodia.

Thirty Bangladeshi workers have returned to Dhaka after being released from the Immigration Detention Centre in Phnom Penh, Cambodia.

The workers arrived at Shahjalal International Airport on Tuesday afternoon via a Thai Airways flight.

They had originally traveled to Cambodia in search of employment but became trapped in scam centres within the country.

While the Cambodian government offered repatriation without fines, immigration police detained 32 people during checks on September 3.

Two individuals were released, while the remaining 30 were held in the detention centre due to irregular status and other complications.

The Anirban Survivor Voice Foundation applied for their release, prompting the Bangladesh Embassy in Bangkok to intervene.

Following diplomatic efforts and the completion of required procedures, the 30 workers were finally secured and repatriated.

headline_marked: PM Tarique Rahman [[makes first official visit to Rajshahi]]
headline: PM Tarique Rahman makes first official visit to Rajshahi
summary: The Prime Minister arrived in the city for a public rally at Madrasa Field, calling for unity among all faiths to build the nation.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman arrived at Rajshahi's Shah Makhdum Airport on Tuesday afternoon via military aircraft, marking his first official visit to the city since taking office.
The Prime Minister directly attended a public rally at the historic Madrasa Field, where he addressed the crowd as the chief guest.
During his visit, the Prime Minister called for the unity of all faiths to build a desired Bangladesh, emphasizing inclusivity and national cohesion.
The visit also included a program to distribute incentive funds among sugarcane farmers in the Rajshahi region.
Prior to arriving in Rajshahi, the Prime Minister had visited the Radha Govinda Temple in Rangpur earlier that morning.
Local leaders, including MP Mohammad Shofiqul Haque Milon, plan to use the visit to present demands for the city's development, including the establishment of a full-fledged agricultural university.

Other key demands include upgrading the airport to a full international airport, establishing an agricultural export processing zone (EPZ), and completing the construction of Rajshahi Medical University.
The city saw extensive preparations for the visit, including road repairs, drainage work, and the city's official designation as the 'City of Education' to be formally requested.
caption:
PM Tarique Rahman visits Rajshahi for the first time since taking office, calling for interfaith unity.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman arrived at Rajshahi's Shah Makhdum Airport on Tuesday afternoon via military aircraft, marking his first official visit to the city since taking office.

The Prime Minister directly attended a public rally at the historic Madrasa Field, where he addressed the crowd as the chief guest.

During his visit, the Prime Minister called for the unity of all faiths to build a desired Bangladesh, emphasizing inclusivity and national cohesion.

The visit also included a program to distribute incentive funds among sugarcane farmers in the Rajshahi region.

Prior to arriving in Rajshahi, the Prime Minister had visited the Radha Govinda Temple in Rangpur earlier that morning.

Local leaders, including MP Mohammad Shofiqul Haque Milon, plan to use the visit to present demands for the city's development, including the establishment of a full-fledged agricultural university.

Other key demands include upgrading the airport to a full international airport, establishing an agricultural export processing zone (EPZ), and completing the construction of Rajshahi Medical University.

The city saw extensive preparations for the visit, including road repairs, drainage work, and the city's official designation as the 'City of Education' to be formally requested.
